messages:
aditi: terraform apply finished for eu-west-2/gpu-nodegroup but 6/8 nodes are NotReady. aws-node pods show crashloop and ENI errors. anyone seen this after a nodegroup rollout?
marcos: oncall? i'm available. can you paste the kubelet/syslogs and the TF snippet you applied?
aditi: gist: the only change was renaming cluster var from "redwood-prod" -> "redwood-main" to match new bootstrap. terraform created new nodegroup in existing subnets but cloud provider can't attach ENIs. logs: 
```
Oct 12 14:02:11 ip-10-0-12-34 kubelet[1234]: failed to get podCIDR from cloud provider: subnet missing tag kubernetes.io/cluster/redwood-main=owned
Oct 12 14:02:12 ip-10-0-12-34 aws-node[987]: error allocating IP: ENI attach failed: subnet not tagged
```
marcos: that explains it — aws cloud-controller expects the cluster tag on subnets. if the subnets are still tagged for redwood-prod the controller will ignore them. did the TF that created the new nodegroup touch subnet tags?
aditi: No, subnets were managed in a different repo. I assumed tags were generic. i can run a quick tag apply but worried about race with Argo sync.
sela: FYI gitops reported a reconcile error earlier: 
infra-bot: [ARGO] sync failed: overlay/eu-west-2/cluster/subnets - kustomize apply: resource patch failed (missing field)
marcos: easy fix: add the tag `kubernetes.io/cluster/redwood-main` to the three subnets, then restart aws-node DaemonSet on the affected nodes. That should let CCM/eni attach and pods go Ready. After that nodes should register with autoscaler.
aditi: can we do that without touching prod? These subnets are shared with other clusters. tagging wrong cluster name could break others.
jess: we should be careful. if other clusters relied on `redwood-prod` tag then changing tags might confuse them. check which clusters are actually using those subnets: 
```bash
aws ec2 describe-tags --filters "Name=resource-type,Values=subnet" "Name=key,Values=kubernetes.io/cluster/*" --region eu-west-2
```
We might add both tags (`redwood-prod` and `redwood-main`) temporarily.
tom: alternative: patch TF in the nodegroup repo to set `kubernetes.io/cluster = redwood-prod` to match subnet tags, then re-create with that cluster name. downside: inconsistent naming. better: tag subnets with both keys and open a cleanup ticket.
aditi: cost question — if we keep both nodegroups up while we fix, we double GPU spend. can we cordon/drain the older pool and scale it to 0 to avoid overlap? autoscaler respects taints but we have guaranteed pods pinned to specific nodeSelector for gpu-type.
marcos: we can scale old pool to 0 for a short window. if any pods are pinned we might need to migrate them. suggest: 1) tag subnets with redwood-main (and keep redwood-prod), 2) restart aws-node, 3) drain older GPU pool and scale to 0, 4) patch TF to unify cluster name and plan a tidy-up.
sela: also check the addon helm release values — argo shows `aws-node` helm chart diff about serviceAccount name change. If serviceAccount name changed, rollout will keep crashing pods until we reconcile RBAC.
aditi: here's the minimal terraform patch I ran: 
```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu" {
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name # changed from "redwood-prod" to "redwood-main"
  node_group_name = "gpu-p-1"
  subnet_ids = var.gpu_subnets
}
```
marcos: ok that's the root cause. for a quick recovery: add the new tag on subnets, `kubectl rollout restart daemonset aws-node -n kube-system` and watch `kubectl get nodes`; if ENI attached nodes should move to Ready.
jess: i'll prep the terraform change in infra-subnets repo to add both tags and open a PR with a rollback note. also notify networking team before tagging.
aditi: i'll do the subnet tag and restart now. i'll post status. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [CI] New incident created: INF-2026-298 — gpu nodegroup provisioning failure (linked to argo sync failure).
aditi: update — tagged subnets with `kubernetes.io/cluster/redwood-main=owned` and restarted aws-node. 4 nodes transitioned to Ready within 10m, 2 are still pending ENI attach. coordinating with cloud infra for quota check.
tom: we should also add a preflight check in our nodegroup pipeline to validate subnet tags before apply. open a GH issue for rollout automation guardrails.
aditi: created issue #4823 with checklist: subnet tag validation, cross-repo change window, cost impact notice. i'll coordinate with networking and schedule a cleanup to remove duplicate tags after consolidation.
marcos: thanks — nice triage. once all nodes Ready i'll run a quick smoke test and scale old pool down to 0 to avoid extra GPU costs.
